item.title: Sutton Bridge man completes wing walk for Queen Elizabeth Hospital
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Sutton Bridge man completes wing walk for Queen Elizabeth Hospital
A Sutton Bridge man has raised £1,200 for the endoscopy unit at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. Brian Moss completed a sponsored wing walk at Wickenby Airfield last month to thank staff for the care his wife received at the hospital late last year.
Mr. Moss was supported in his fundraising by family, friends, and his colleagues at Bridge Hardware, who contributed through sponsorship and a World Cup sweepstake. Lead nurse manager Helen Smith thanked Mr. Moss for his efforts, noting that the funds will help enhance patient care. Those interested in supporting the hospital charity can find more information on the Queen Elizabeth Hospital website.

item.title: Historic cobblestones restored at King’s Lynn museum
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Historic cobblestones restored at King’s Lynn museum
The first phase of a restoration project at True’s Yard Fisherfolk Museum in King’s Lynn is now complete. Volunteers from the Lynn and West Norfolk Archaeological Society spent two weeks uncovering and restoring original cobblestones in the museum’s courtyard. The historic flooring was discovered after the removal of the Activity vessel, which has since been relocated to Dersingham.
The work has revealed the thresholds of previously demolished cottages, offering a glimpse into the lives of local fishing families from a century ago. Museum officials say the project was made possible through grants and private donations. Future plans for the site include building replica cottages for educational use, an initiative estimated to cost £500,000.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/go-back-100-years-in-time-as-cobblestones-as-fisherfolk-muse-9482782/

item.title: King’s Lynn Corn Exchange to light up for domestic abuse charity
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn Corn Exchange to light up for domestic abuse charity
The King’s Lynn-based Pandora Project is marking its 13th anniversary with a special illumination of the town’s Corn Exchange. The building will be lit in purple this Saturday, September 19, ahead of Domestic Abuse Awareness Month in October.
The charity provides specialist support to women and children across North and West Norfolk affected by domestic abuse. Figures from Norfolk County Council show nearly 11,400 domestic abuse-related crimes were recorded in the county during 2023/24. Organisers hope the display will raise awareness and remind those in need that local support services remain available. Further information can be found on the Pandora Project website.

Ely records highest safety improvements from 20mph speed limits
New data indicates that the introduction of a 20mph speed limit in Ely has resulted in the most significant road safety improvements across Cambridgeshire. According to reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, the lower speed restrictions have proven more effective in the city than in other parts of the county. Local residents and commuters are advised that these measures continue to impact traffic flow and safety standards throughout the area.
